newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude strong but mogas is weak lin.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude strong but mogas is weak lin.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ NYMEX crude oil looks strong after Monday's impressive recovery and next resistance is seen at $19.25 a barrel.
+ Gasoline is the weak link in the markets and has room to fall to as low as 52.00 cents a gallon.

NYMEX crude oil futures are looking strong as a result of an impressive recovery on Monday but gloom still surrounds the gasoline market and this could exert downwards pressure on the markets, traders and technical analysts said.
"Yesterday's reversal was pretty powerful," said one Washington-based chart analyst. "We travelled under $19.00, which is an important psychological level, and then came back up again."
First resistance would kick in, she said, at $19.25, roughly the level of Monday's high. Above that lies $19.60.
"In the longer term we are holding out for a bottom to this market at $18.00," she added.
Gasoline was not looking so healthy, however, except possibly in the short term.
"We have oversold conditions...the recovery we saw yesterday was impressive," she said, but added, "I think 56.50 cents will hold this market for now."
"Momentum is so solidly down - ultimately I see this market moving down to 52.00."
Charles Gray at Prudential-Bache Futures in London also thought gasoline could provide a stumbling block.

"Unleaded mogas keeps its position as the weak link in the market," he said. "There is a potential flag pattern here that implies 53.00 cents, but other falling wedge patterns in gas oil, heat and WTI contradict this."
"Will the cavalry come to the rescue?"
But he said Monday's close was very constructive and added: "Despite opportunities to go lower the market has failed (to do so,) so a rally is a fair outcome."
